previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, and morbid obesity was admitted after being found unresponsive, with hypercarbic respiratory failure. She had not taken her medications or used her CPAP for several days. She was treated with BIPAP, IV diuresis with Lasix, and a steroid taper for COPD exacerbation and acute on chronic heart failure. Her mental status and respiratory function improved, and she was weaned off BIPAP. The Lasix dose was increased to twice daily, prednisone was started on a taper, and isosorbide mononitrate was discontinued. She was discharged back to assisted living with stable vital signs, clear lungs, and no need for home oxygen, with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ woman with a pmhx. significant for OSA, 
CHF, HTN admitted for hypercarbic respiratory failure, left 
against medical advice after evaluation by psychiatry.
.
#  HYPERCAPNIC RESPIRTORY FAILURE:  Patient with chronic 
hypercapnia due to untreated OSA and COPD (increased v/q 
mismatch) as well as hypoxia from volume overload.  Altered 
mental status in setting of hypercarbia.  Unclear precipitant 
for this acute episode, though CHF was likely playing a role.  
Patient has a history of non-compliance with medications (i.e. 
diuretics) and her dietary history is not known.  Unlikely to be 
PNA without a fever, white count, or sputum production.  COPD 
exacerbation is likely also contributing, though patient does 
not sound that tight or wheezy on exam.  In the ICU, Ms. ___ 
___ was diuresed with good effect.  She was continued on 
steroids and frequent nebuilizers.  Ms. ___ was 
encouraged to use BiPap but she refused.  She also refused ABGs 
in the ICU.  She was transferred to the medicine floor, and 
agreed to wear bipap overnight.  On the second day on the 
medical floor, she insisted on leaving ""AMA.""  Psychiatry was 
called to reassess capacity.  She was determined to have 
capacity after it was confimred with assisted living that she 
does have a nurse who dispenses medications.  She left with 
instructions to take lasix 60mg twice daily and prednisone 
taper.  She was encouraged to stop smoking and wear nicotine 
patch.  She was aware of the risk of recurrent hypercarbic 
respiratory failure and possible death if she did not stay in 
the hospital to continue therapy.
.
# CHF, acute diastolic:  Preserved EF with evidence of diastolic 
dysfunction.  Likely volume overload contributing to this 
current presentation.  It's unclear how compliant patient has 
been with current cardiac medications and/or heart failure diet. 
 Patient was continued on ASA, ACE-I, BB, statin, diuretics, and 
imdur.  She was given lasix boluses while in the ICU.  She was 
discharged with instructions to take lasix BID.
.
# HYPERTENSION:  Patient was continued on ACE-I, BB, diuretics, 
and lasix.
.
# DM2, uncontrolled with complications:  Insulin sliding scale 
during admission, discharged with metformin only.  Patient may 
benefit from insulin upon discharge.
.
# DEPRESSION:  Fluoxetine and aripiprazole were continued.
.
# GERD:  Omeprazole was continued.
